diet.title: Diet and Lifestyle
diet.description: Explore general food ideas, build a simple daily meal plan, and track meals and water. Choose what feels comfortable and follow your care team's advice.
diet.disclaimer: General guidance, not a replacement for a doctor or dietitian.
diet.reviewPending: These sample suggestions are awaiting clinician review and must not be treated as approved clinical guidance.
diet.healthDisclaimer: Food suggestions do not prevent, diagnose, or treat oral cancer. If swallowing or breathing is difficult, seek emergency help now.
diet.preferenceNote: Turn this off to include non-vegetarian meal options alongside vegetarian choices.

stageTips.prevention: Choose a varied diet that suits you. Avoid tobacco, betel quid/gutka, and alcohol; food choices do not replace regular dental or clinical care.
stageTips.screening: Eating well does not change a screening result. Continue your planned clinician visits and ask a dietitian about individual nutrition needs.
stageTips.postTreatment: Follow your oncologist's or dietitian's instructions. Treatment can change texture, energy, protein, and fluid needs; these general meal ideas may not fit your plan.

softFoods.title: Soft, moist foods
softFoods.description: If your mouth is sore, consider soft rice, idli, porridge, khichdi, dal, curd, or well-cooked vegetables, as tolerated.

fruitVegetables.title: Fruits and vegetables
fruitVegetables.description: Choose ripe, soft fruits or cooked vegetables. Mash or soften them if that is more comfortable.

protein.title: Protein sources
protein.description: Options include lentils, beans, eggs, milk or curd, paneer, tofu, fish, or tender chicken, depending on your preferences and care plan.

energyFoods.title: Nourishing meal additions
energyFoods.description: Rice, oats, ragi porridge, and other familiar grains can be made softer with dal, milk, or broth when suitable for you.

tobacco.title: Tobacco
tobacco.description: Avoid smoking and smokeless tobacco products. Ask a clinician for help with quitting.

betel.title: Betel quid, areca nut, and gutka
betel.description: Avoid betel quid, areca/supari, gutka, and similar products.

alcohol.title: Alcohol
alcohol.description: Avoid alcohol, especially if your care team has advised against it or your mouth is sore.

irritants.title: Irritating foods when the mouth is sore
irritants.description: Avoid very spicy, very hot, or acidic foods if they sting or worsen discomfort.

roughFoods.title: Rough or sharp foods when the mouth is sore
roughFoods.description: Avoid hard crisps, sharp toast, and rough foods that scrape or hurt.

diet.mealIdeasDescription: These are examples, not a prescribed diet. Choose familiar foods that you can comfortably eat.

meals.idliDescription: Try soft idli with mild dal or curd; avoid spicy accompaniments if they irritate your mouth.
meals.pesarattuDescription: A moong-dal option; make it soft and use a mild accompaniment if comfortable.
meals.softEggDescription: Soft-cooked egg with moist rice, if eggs suit your diet and care plan.
meals.daliaDescription: Cook wheat or other suitable grains until soft; choose a savory or mild version.
meals.softRiceDescription: A familiar soft rice dish; add well-cooked lentils if they suit you.
meals.khichdiDescription: Soft rice, lentils, and well-cooked vegetables; keep seasoning mild if your mouth is sore.
meals.dalRiceDescription: A familiar protein-containing meal. Moisten well and choose mild seasoning.
meals.softFishRiceDescription: Well-cooked, boneless fish with soft rice, if fish suits your diet and care plan.
meals.softChickenRiceDescription: Tender, well-cooked chicken in a mild preparation with soft rice, if suitable for you.
meals.curdRiceDescription: A soft, moist option if dairy suits you. Avoid it if your care team has advised otherwise.
meals.softRotiDalDescription: Soften roti with dal or gravy if chewing is comfortable; choose another texture if not.
meals.eggStewRiceDescription: Soft-cooked egg in a mild, moist preparation with rice, if suitable for you.
meals.fruitYogurtDescription: Use ripe, soft fruit and plain curd if tolerated; avoid acidic fruit if it stings.

diet.swallowingTips: Tips for mouth pain or difficulty swallowing
diet.swallowingTip1: If eating is comfortable, try small bites and soft, moist foods. Stop if swallowing causes pain or feels unsafe.
diet.swallowingTip2: Do not force food or drink. Ask a clinician promptly about new or worsening pain, choking, or difficulty swallowing.
diet.swallowingTip3: If you have trouble breathing or cannot swallow, call 112 now. Do not wait for a meal plan or app response.
diet.hydrationDescription: Take sips as comfortable and follow any fluid instructions from your clinician. If you have been told to limit fluids, follow that advice.

evaluationWorkflow.title: Evaluation workflow
evaluationWorkflow.description: The evaluation sheet expects an end-to-end patient journey linking registration, screening, clinical review, referrals, treatment tracking, and dashboards. This page maps that expected journey to what is currently connected in this simulation.
evaluationWorkflow.simulationNotice: SIMULATION ONLY. This is a workflow and implementation-status guide, not a clinical service or a promise that every step is operational.
evaluationWorkflow.journeyDescription: Follow each stage in order. Entry links open existing sign-in screens; a successful sign-in is required for protected role features.

registration.title: 1. Patient registration and consent
registration.description: A health worker can record a patient and catchment details with separate screening, photo, and data-sharing choices. Patient OTP sign-in and the consent centre are also present.
registration.owner: Entry role: health worker or patient

screening.title: 2. Symptom questionnaire and screening record
screening.description: The API provides a configurable questionnaire and saves answers with screening consent. A complete patient-facing wizard, image capture quality guidance, and connected screening dashboard are not yet present.

imageAi.title: 3. Oral photo quality and advisory AI
imageAi.description: The server has an advisory Gemini provider and safety tests, but no patient screening-image API/UI connects capture, image quality checks, analysis, and report delivery end to end.
imageAi.owner: Expected: patient capture, server analysis, advisory-only result

doctorReview.title: 4. Clinician review and teleconsultation
doctorReview.description: Care and video data models and some API operations exist. The doctor dashboard is still a placeholder; case review, AI override, specialist consultation, and released clinical notes are not integrated into a working UI journey.

referralTracking.title: 5. Referral, diagnostics, and treatment tracking
referralTracking.description: Navigator queues and investigation-state tracking APIs and screens are available. They are not yet connected to a complete doctor-reviewed referral and patient follow-up path.
referralTracking.owner: Entry role: navigator; clinical classification must remain clinician-only

dashboard.title: 6. Aggregate care dashboard
dashboard.description: District aggregate dashboard and CSV export are implemented with groups under five suppressed and no patient identifiers. It requires an authorized district-officer account.

evaluationWorkflow.criteriaDescription: These are the seven criteria and weights printed in the supplied PDF. Statuses are a code/UI review, not scores awarded by a judge.
evaluationWorkflow.assessmentNote: Important gaps for the live demonstration: the patient screening-to-image-AI flow and the doctor review/teleconsultation UI are not connected. Do not present these as completed or use this simulation for real patient care.

offline.title: Offline-first care access
offline.emergencyText: Severe symptoms require urgent care. Use the emergency icon, label, and colour to act quickly; do not wait for AI output.
offline.logout: Clear local offline data and log out
